newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch say flawed data explains "hidden" copper.
newsitem.headline: Dutch say flawed data explains "hidden" copper.

text.p: The Dutch Statistical Office (CBS) said on Wednesday the data it supplied to the World Bureau of Metal Statistics (WBMS) last month indicating the possibility of "hidden" copper stocks in Rotterdam was flawed.

The CBS told Reuters the inaccuracies in its data completely explained the conclusion drawn by WBMS that over 5OO,000 tonnes of copper could not be accounted for and was possibly lying in Rotterdam warehouses.

The WBMS report was based on data from the CBS and the London Metal Exchange over a five-year period between 1990 and 1995. A discrepency arose between the official Dutch import and export figures and stocks of copper reported to the LME.
The CBS has conducted a three-week investigation into the data it supplied and said the results seemed to solve the puzzle of the "missing" copper.
"The amounts fully match up," a spokesman for the CBS told Reuters. "This accounts for the copper."
In a statement the CBS said the main reason for the problem was a failure to pinpoint copper flows to and from the port.
